speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg, including when it first appeared, any changes in size or appearance, and if you have noticed any fever or swollen lymph nodes. Also, do you have a history of diabetes, immunosuppression, or recent insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent corticosteroid use, your immune system may not be able to fight off the parasite from that ant bite. I need to confirm the diagnosis with a biopsy before we begin treatment. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy. REQUEST IMAGES: Lesion_Close_Up.
